question: What released ActionBench input semantics can be checked prospectively after immutable snapshot admission, without turning an engineering check into scientific qualification?

observed_claims: 16 RGBA frames with alpha mask per sample
first three columns are positions and final three are normals
camera uses Blender convention and points to the released projection.py
all frames are selected from the tensor first dimension
only the first three columns are consumed as positions by the scorer
camera keys are R, T, focal_length_ndc and principal_point_ndc
R is used as a 3x3 rotation and T as a length-3 translation
focal length and principal point each have two components
projection uses X_cam = points @ R.T + T and a -Z viewing direction
the released JSON contains exactly the four projection keys
the observed R, T, focal and principal-point values match the published shapes
sources.scope_limit: One browsed example supports schema inspection but not population-wide validity; the generated Local pass checks all 128.

observed_claims: sample directories expose camera.json, surfaces.npy and imgs
the inspected imgs tree contains 00.png through 15.png

review_decisions: Check only semantics needed by released input and evaluator code; do not invent a normal-length or alpha-occupancy threshold.
Revalidate every consumed file against the prior snapshot admission before parsing, so a post-admission mutation fails closed.
Treat tracked correspondence as a documented source property, not something this structural pass independently proves.
Keep this as purpose=engineering, CPU-only, single-attempt and output-preserving.
Do not count successful input semantics as native scorer qualification, a baseline result, a candidate result or dispatch readiness.
